name: Andhra Pradesh
description: Known for its rich history, classical dance forms like Kuchipudi, ancient Buddhist heritage sites, and the famous Tirupati Balaji temple.

name: Arunachal Pradesh
description: The land of the dawn-lit mountains, home to diverse tribal cultures, Buddhist monasteries, and pristine natural landscapes.

name: Assam
description: Famous for its tea gardens, Kaziranga National Park, Kamakhya Temple, and the classical dance form Sattriya.

name: Bihar
description: The cradle of Buddhism and Jainism, home to Bodh Gaya, Nalanda University ruins, and the Mahabodhi Temple Complex.

name: Chhattisgarh
description: Rich in tribal culture, waterfalls, ancient temples, and Bastar art. Known for Chitrakote Falls and Bhoramdeo Temple.
temples: Bhoramdeo, Rajim Rajiv Lochan, Sirpur Laxman

name: Goa
description: Home to UNESCO-listed Churches and Convents of Old Goa, Portuguese colonial heritage, and vibrant coastal culture.

name: Gujarat
description: Land of the UNESCO-listed Rani ki Vav stepwell, Dholavira of the Indus Valley Civilization, and the vibrant Navratri festival.

name: Haryana
description: Site of the historic Kurukshetra battlefield, mentioned in the Mahabharata. Rich in Haryanvi folk traditions and crafts.
temples: Brahma Sarovar, Mata Mansa Devi, Jyotisar

name: Himachal Pradesh
description: Himalayan state with magnificent Buddhist monasteries, colonial hill stations, and ancient temples in the Kullu-Manali valley.

name: Jharkhand
description: Land of forests with tribal heritage, ancient rock art at Hazaribagh, and Deoghar Shiva temple, one of the 12 Jyotirlingas.

name: Karnataka
description: Home to the UNESCO-listed Hampi ruins, Hoysala temples, Mysuru palace, and vibrant Carnatic music and Yakshagana tradition.

name: Kerala
description: God's Own Country — famous for Kathakali dance, backwaters, ancient Guruvayur temple, and Mattancherry's Jewish heritage.

name: Madhya Pradesh
description: The heart of India with UNESCO sites Khajuraho, Sanchi Stupa, Bhimbetka rock shelters, and diverse tribal heritage.

name: Maharashtra
description: Home to UNESCO-listed Ajanta and Ellora Caves, Elephanta Caves, and the Maratha empire's magnificent fort heritage.
temples: Trimbakeshwar, Shirdi Sai Baba, Pandharpur Vitthal

name: Manipur
description: Birthplace of Polo, known for Meitei culture, the classical Manipuri dance form, and the sacred Loktak Lake.

name: Meghalaya
description: The abode of clouds, known for living root bridges, Khasi tribal culture, and the wettest place on Earth, Mawsynram.

name: Mizoram
description: A harmonious land of Mizo tribal culture, bamboo crafts, and stunning scenic landscapes in the northeastern hills.

name: Nagaland
description: Famous for Hornbill Festival, Naga tribal heritage, warrior traditions, and the historic Battle of Kohima site.

name: Odisha
description: Temple of Temples — home to the UNESCO-listed Konark Sun Temple, Puri Jagannath Temple, and the classical Odissi dance.
temples: Jagannath Puri, Lingaraj, Konark Sun Temple

name: Punjab
description: Land of five rivers and the Golden Temple in Amritsar — one of India's most revered Sikh shrines, drawing millions yearly.

name: Rajasthan
description: The land of royals with UNESCO-listed hill forts, vibrant folk music and dance, Jaipur's Pink City, and Thar desert heritage.
temples: Brahma Temple Pushkar, Karni Mata, Eklingji

name: Sikkim
description: A Himalayan jewel with ancient Buddhist monasteries, Rumtek Monastery, and Kangchenjunga, India's highest peak.

name: Tamil Nadu
description: Home to UNESCO-listed Mahabalipuram monuments, Brihadeeswarar Temple, classical Bharatanatyam dance, and Carnatic music.

name: Telangana
description: Known for Charminar, Golconda Fort, Warangal's Kakatiya temple ruins, and its pearl and Bidri craft heritage.

name: Tripura
description: Rich in Bengali and tribal culture with the 14th-century Ujjayanta Palace, Neermahal palace, and Tripura Sundari temple.

name: Uttar Pradesh
description: Home to UNESCO-listed Taj Mahal, Agra Fort, Fatehpur Sikri, Varanasi ghats, and the Ayodhya Ram Janmabhoomi.
temples: Kashi Vishwanath, Ayodhya Ram Mandir, Mathura

name: Uttarakhand
description: Devbhumi — land of gods with Char Dham pilgrimage sites, Haridwar and Rishikesh on the sacred Ganga, and Himalayan culture.

name: West Bengal
description: Cultural capital with Durga Puja UNESCO recognition, Rabindranath Tagore's heritage, Sundarbans, and Bishnupur temples.

name: Delhi
description: Capital territory with UNESCO-listed Red Fort, Qutub Minar complex, Humayun's Tomb, and millennia of layered history.
temples: Akshardham, Lotus Temple, Birla Mandir, Kalkaji

name: Jammu and Kashmir
description: Paradise on Earth — home to the Amarnath cave shrine, Vaishno Devi temple, Kashmir Valley, and ancient Martand Sun Temple.
temples: Mata Vaishno Devi, Amarnath Cave, Shankaracharya

name: Ladakh
description: The land of high passes with ancient Tibetan Buddhist monasteries, Hemis Monastery, and Pangong Tso lake.

name: Puducherry
description: French colonial heritage meets Tamil culture in this coastal UT, home to Sri Aurobindo Ashram and Auroville.

name: Andaman and Nicobar Islands
description: Historic Cellular Jail, pristine beaches, Andamanese tribal culture, and rich marine biodiversity in the Bay of Bengal.

name: Lakshadweep
description: Coral island territory with unique Islamic heritage, traditional boat-building crafts, and vibrant Lakshadweep folk dances.

name: Chandigarh
description: Le Corbusier's planned city featuring the iconic Rock Garden, Sukhna Lake, and its unique modernist architectural heritage.

name: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
description: Portuguese colonial heritage, tribal Warli art, ancient temples, and coastal traditions blend in these western union territories.
